reviews.title: Very Impressed
reviews.comment: I was very interested in trying a glass pad for the first time. I am an avid gamer (Valorant, Siege, Apex, CS etc…). I used to have the original Razer Firefly. I loved the hard mouse pad texture, however, the size was too small for me. I switched to a generic desk size cloth pad from Corsair. I am not a fan of cloth pads but I loved the size. The Razer Atlas Pro is a perfect size for me. It is shockingly thin and feels great without a sleeve. I have never left a review before, but I am very impressed with this mouse pad. Yes, it is pricey, but this product is worth it to me after using it for a month.
reviews.author: Sean Carver

reviews.title: smooth and responsive
reviews.comment: This Pro Tempered Glass Gaming Mouse Mat arrived well-packaged and protected.  The 1.9mm completely exceeded my expectations. The tempered glass surface feels incredibly smooth and responsive, making mouse movements fast, accurate, and effortless during gaming sessions. The glass surface gives my setup a clean, modern appearance.  It feels sturdy and durable without taking up too much desk space. The base stays firmly in place.  Another big plus is how easy it is to clean.
reviews.author: Family

reviews.title: Exactly what I hoped for
reviews.comment: It's super thin. You can lay your arm across the edge and not really feel the transition. The surface is similar to the original Atlas, but maybe a little less scratchy sounding. I am not sure as I use a different mouse at that location.  Both are faster and smoother than cloth.  It's bigger than the original. I have a full sized keyboard and a six foot wide desk. It fits, but only with an inch and a half to spare. Measure before you buy.  Or use a TKL or 75% keyboard.
reviews.author: RunForTheHills

reviews.title: Son highly recommends!!
reviews.comment: My son loves the glass mouse pad! Say it has less drag with using mouse pads when playing Fortnite!
reviews.author: Laura

reviews.title: My First Glass Mousepad!
reviews.comment:
I have always wanted to try tempered glass mousepads as it is the only kind I have not gotten to test out yet. I am a fan of using Razer products and I will say it was absolutely cool to try out.
First, I'll mention that that it is larger than I thought it would be. It isnt large like a desk one. But it is larger than a standard mousepad, hopefully they will release other sizes, such as one the same size as their Firefly which is a standard size mousepad, as this one will struggle to fit on smaller desks. This isn't their fault, it's mine for not measuring my desk space. To test this out, I needed to move all of my other peripherals to the left.
Next, it will take some getting used to if you are not familiar with using tempered glass, the friction and glide is a different experience from fabric and hard mousepads. For example, I play a variety of games such as Final Fantasy XIV, Arc Raiders, Marvel Rivals and other games. Currently, I'm on a FFXIV binge again.
I mainly use the Razer Naga Pro, with the interchangeable side plates and love it. So that is what I tested this mousepad with.
I didn't experience any issues with any of the game genres and generally, it had a very smooth glide, my mouse skates may be wearing out though so there was a bit of drag depending on how much I moved the mouse. I would say this type of mousepad is best suited for games that require pinpoint movement like FPS.
The mousepad itself is very thin as in, very flat. But it does not feel flimsy or like it will break. I do however, worry that over time, it will get scratched or wear out my mouse skates which I experienced with the Razer Firefly V2 due to its textured surface. But that is my own paranoia.
Overall, take awesome mousepad, I recommend it for both people who are experienced with tempered glass or are new to them like me. Just make sure you have the space for it. I'll keep using it until I get more comfortable with it and I'll figure the desk out... I need a new desk anyway at some point. :(
reviews.author: K
